Recommendations for management of patien: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of CV events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death. (Class I)
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM and HFrEF to reduce hospitalizations for HF and CV death. (Class I)
The DPP-4 inhibitor saxagliptin is not recommended in patients with HF. (Class III)
All patients with HF should be periodically screened for anaemia and iron deficiency with a full blood count, serum ferritin concentration, and TSAT. (Class I)

Intravenous iron supplementation with ferric carboxymaltose should be considered in symptomatic HF patients recently hospitalized for HF with LVEF ≤50% and iron deficiency (serum ferritin <100 ng/mL or ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%) to reduce risk of HF hospitalization. (Class IIa)
Treatment of anaemia in HF with erythropoietin stimulating agents is not recommended in the absence of other indications. (Class III)

Cancer patients at increased risk for cardiotoxicity should undergo CV evaluation before scheduled anticancer therapy, preferably by a cardiologist with experience/interest in Cardio-Oncology. (Class I)
Treatment with an ACE‑I and a beta-blocker (preferably carvedilol) should be considered in cancer patients developing LV systolic dysfunction during anthracycline chemotherapy. (Class IIa)
A baseline CV risk assessment should be considered in all cancer patients scheduled to receive cancer treatment with potential to cause HF. (Class IIa)
Recommendations for treatment of patient: Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetic testing–proven hATTR‑CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality. (Class I)
Tafamidis is recommended in patients with wtTTR‑CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms and CV hospitalization. (Class I)

Associated Conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
